lines: Meet MeetingScribe.
It turns your Teams, Zoom and Google Meet calls into clean notes, and now into Jira tickets.
Without anything leaving your computer, unless you say so.
Meetings create work.
But notes go unwritten, action items get lost, and the tickets never get raised.
MeetingScribe runs quietly in the background.
When you join a call, it starts recording two tracks: your microphone, and the meeting's own audio.
No buttons to press, and no bot joining the meeting.
It works with the meetings you already have: the Teams and Zoom apps, and Google Meet in your browser.
Teams and Zoom on the web, Webex, Jitsi and Whereby work in the browser too.
In a browser, it waits for two signals: the browser is using the microphone, and a meeting tab is open.
Then it records only the browser's sound, and names the note after the meeting.
Dictating a document, or recording a voice message, is never mistaken for a call.
When the call ends, everything runs right on your computer.
Whisper transcribes both tracks.
Voiceprints tell the speakers apart, and recognise people it has heard before.
A local language model drops the small talk, then writes the summary and the action items.
A few minutes later, a Markdown note lands in your Meeting Notes folder.
Who was there, what was decided, and who owes what.
An unknown voice? Name it once.
From the next meeting on, it is recognised automatically.
And now, the new part.
MeetingScribe can turn those action items into Jira tickets, with you approving every one.
Run control jira, and sign in with a personal access token, an API token, or your browser's session cookie for single sign-on sites.
It can stay in your Mac's Keychain or in Windows Credential Manager, and you are asked again when it expires.
Then tell it which Jira space new tickets should go to.
The same local model reads the meeting, and pulls out the work that belongs in Jira.
Owners, due dates, and the keywords to search for.
Then it searches every Jira space you can see, not just your own.
Each ticket it finds is compared with the new work: the same deliverable, merely related, or unrelated.
Work that already has an open ticket gets a comment, not a duplicate.
Genuinely new work gets a new ticket, linked to its relatives.
And if a closed ticket's problem is back, it opens a fresh one, and links the history.
Every field is filled in from the conversation, and checked against what your Jira space allows.
Type, priority, assignee, due date, components, even required custom fields.
Nothing is pushed until you say yes, and you can edit any field first.
Say yes, and it is on the board.
The comments are posted, and the meeting note links to every ticket.
Use it for stand-ups, migration syncs, incident reviews, sprint planning, and stakeholder calls.
Anywhere talk turns into work.
Recording, transcription, and every model stay on your computer.
The only thing that leaves is the Jira update you approved, sent straight to your own Jira site.
MeetingScribe runs on Apple Silicon Macs and on Windows PCs.
Both install with one command. On Windows it runs on the processor, or on an NVIDIA graphics card if you have one.
Install it once, join your meetings as usual, and review the tickets when you are ready.
MeetingScribe. Meetings, written down, and followed up.
